TRANSCREATION, NOT TRANSLATION (2026-07-14 pass). English is the reference for MEANING only — do not mirror its syntax, em-dashes or word choices. Per-locale rules: (1) slide1/2 eyebrow = the locale's native 'dual subtitles' search term from docs/keywords-by-language.md (slide 1 mirrors the query the user typed, e.g. fr SOUS-TITRES BILINGUES, hu DUPLA FELIRAT, th ซับสองภาษา, fa دوزبانه, id SUBTITLE DUA BAHASA); (2) 'one tap' → the locale's native desktop CLICK idiom (это десктопное расширение: клик/Klick/clic/clique/kliknięcie/一键/ワンクリック…), never touchscreen 'tap' calques; (3) slide3 callout + any in-copy mode name must match the product UI string ytModeGuess in _locales//messages.json (ru «Угадай», bg „Познай“, zh_CN 猜词, hi अनुमान, sw kukisia…); (4) keep register: sentence case, no slang, adult credible tool; (5) layout budgets — title ≤ ~22 chars per
-line (slide1 ≤ ~36 total, slide4 ≤ ~45 total), sub ≤ ~130 chars, callout ≤ ~30 chars (white-space: nowrap), eyebrow is NOT auto-uppercased by CSS so caps live here in the JSON. SLIDE 5 (new, the built-in dictionary) — read this before touching it. (a) THE TWO STEPS ARE THE POINT AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME STEP. Hovering a word opens a small card: one part-of-speech tag and a few translations, nothing more. The FULL entry — every sense, the usage examples, the line the word appeared in — opens only when the reader presses the card's second button. Earlier copy said hovering showed the part of speech and the senses; it does not, and that wording is a bug, not a style. Name the button with the locale's own ytLookupMore string from _locales//messages.json (ru «Разбор», de Details…), never a word you invent. (b) NO CHARACTER BUDGET. Earlier passes carried '≤20 chars per line' and it is worthless: the column is 440px and 'Cualquier palabra,' is 18 characters but 473px, while 20 narrow letters fit and 15 wide ones do not. Write the sentence first, break it second, then MEASURE with scratchpad/fitcheck.mjs and re-break what does not fit. Four lines are fine — the block has room below it. (c) WRITE A SENTENCE, NOT THREE FRAGMENTS. The failure this slide keeps producing is telegraphese: 'Любое слово — с ходу понятно', 'Jedes Wort, erklärt', 'Każde słowo — wyjaśnione'. All three are the English skeleton (noun + participle) carried over into languages that do not build phrases that way. Compose a natural sentence in the target language, then break it across lines; never compose to fit the chunks. Naturalness is the primary constraint and length is the secondary one — if they conflict, spend the extra words. (d) THE CHECKS ARE BLIND TO MEANING. Three separate defects passed every automated check: Thai repeated its word for 'meaning' twice, Chinese and Japanese broke a noun phrase down the middle. Re-read your own output as a native speaker would before declaring it done — a line count is not a reading.
